# axiomatic proofs {.divider}

We aim for a characterization of sets of modal formulas valid in different classes of frames. 

We begin with the system $\textsf{K}$ which proves all and only formulas valid in all frames. 

## the minimal normal modal logic $\textsf{K}$ 

**Axioms** include:

  - all substitution instances of axioms of propositional logic
  - all substitution instances of axiom 


      $$
      \begin{array}{lll}
        \textsf{K} & & \Box (p \to q) \to (\Box p \to \Box q)\\
        \end{array}
      $$

. . .

Two **rules of inference**:

  - modus ponenes
    
      $$
      \varphi \to \psi, \varphi / \psi \tag{\textsf{MP}}
      $$
        
  - necessitation
    
      $$
      \varphi / \Box \varphi \tag{\textsf{N}}
      $$

## theorem 

::: {.definition}
A **proof** in $\textsf{K}$ is a finite sequence of modal formulas $(\chi_1, \dots , \chi_n)$ where for each $m \leq n$, the formula $\chi_m$ is either

::: {.incremental}
- an axiom

- an outcome of an application of $\textsf{MP}$ to two prior formulas

- an outcome of an application of $\textsf{N}$ to a prior formula
:::
:::

. . .

::: {style="height: 10px;"}
:::

::: {.definition}
A **theorem** of $\textsf{K}$ is formula $\varphi$ is a formula that appears in the last line of a proof in $\textsf{K}$. We write $\vdash_{\textsf{K}} \varphi$ to indicate that $\varphi$ is a theorem of $\textsf{K}$.
:::

## example {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_{\textsf{K}} \Box p \to \Box (q \to p)$
:::

::: {.proof}
$$
\begin{array}{lll}
1 &  p \to (q \to p) & \textsf{A1}[p/p, (p \to p)/q]\\
2 &  \Box (p \to (q \to p))  & \textsf{N}, 1\\
3 &  \Box (p \to (q \to p)) \to (\Box p \to \Box(q \to p)) & \textsf{K}[p/p, (q \to p)/q]\\
4 &  \Box p \to \Box(q \to p) & \textsf{MP} \ 2, 3\\
\end{array}
$$
:::

## soundness

::: {.theorem}
All theorems of $\textsf{K}$ are valid in the class of all frames.
:::

::: {.proof}
- All substitution instances of tautologies are valid in the class of all frames.
- All substitution instances of $\textsf{K}$ are valid in the class of all frames.
- $\textsf{MP}$ preserves validity in the class of all frames.
- $\textsf{N}$ preserves validity in the class of all frames.
:::


## derived rules of inference


::: {.theorem}
If $\vdash_{\textsf{K}} \varphi_1, \dots, \vdash_{\textsf{K}} \varphi_n$ and $\psi$ is derivable from $\{\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi\}$ in propositional logic, then $\vdash_{\textsf{K}} \psi$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Given the Deduction Theorem for Propositional Logic, if $\psi$ is derivable from $\{ \varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n\}$ in Propositional Logic, then $\varphi_1 \to ( \varphi_2 \to \dots (\varphi_n \to \psi) \dots))$ is a theorem of Propositional Logic and thus one of $\textsf{K}$. By repeated applications of $\textsf{MP}$, $\vdash_K \psi$.
:::

## $\textsf{RK}$ {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
($\textsf{RK}$) \ If $\vdash_K \varphi \to \psi$, then $\vdash_K \Box \varphi \to \Box \psi$
:::

::: {.proof}
We may transform a proof of $\varphi \to \psi$ into a proof of $\Box \varphi \to \Box \psi$.

$$\begin{array}{lllll}
n & & \varphi \to \psi & \\
n+1 & & \Box (\varphi \to \psi) & \textsf{RN} \ n\\
n+2  & & \Box (\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Box \varphi \to \Box \psi) & \textsf{K}[\varphi/p, \psi/q]\\
n+3 & & \Box \varphi \to \Box \psi & \textsf{MP} \ n+1, n+2\\
\end{array}$$
:::

## $\textsf{RK}_\Diamond$ {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
($\textsf{RK}$) \ If $\vdash_K \varphi \to \psi$, then $\vdash_K \Diamond \varphi \to \Diamond \psi$
:::

::: {.proof}
We may transform a proof of $\varphi \to \psi$ into a proof of $\Diamond \varphi \to \Diamond \psi$.

$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
n & & \varphi \to \psi & \\
n+1 & & \neg \psi \to \neg \varphi &  \textsf{PL} \ n\\
n+2 & & \Box \neg \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi & \textsf{RK} \ n+1\\
n+4 & & \neg \Box \neg \varphi \to \neg \Box \neg \psi & \textsf{PL} \ n+4\\
n+5 & & \Diamond \varphi \to \Diamond \psi & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond \ n+5
\end{array}
$$
:::


## theorems of $\textsf{K}$ {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_K \Box (\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Diamond \varphi \to \Diamond \psi)$
:::

::: {.proof}
$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & & (\varphi \to \psi) \to (\neg \psi \to \neg \varphi) & \textsf{PL} \\
2 & & \Box (\varphi \to \psi) \to \Box(\neg \psi \to \neg \varphi) & \textsf{RK} \ 1 \\
3 & & \Box (\neg \psi \to \neg \varphi) \to (\Box \neg \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi) & \textsf{K}[\neg \psi/p, \neg \varphi/q] \\
4 & & (\Box \neg \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi) \to (\neg \Box \neg \varphi \to \neg \Box \neg \psi) & \textsf{PL}\\
5 & & \Box (\varphi \to \psi) \to (\neg \Box \neg \varphi \to \neg \Box \neg \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 2, 3, 4\\
6 & & \Box (\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Diamond \varphi \to \Diamond \psi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond \  6\\
\end{array}
$$
:::


## necessity commutes with conjunction ($\Rightarrow$) {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_K \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to (\Box \varphi \wedge \Box \psi)$
:::

::: {.proof}
\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & & (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \varphi & \textsf{PL} \\
2 & & \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \Box \varphi & \textsf{RK} \ 1 \\
3 & & (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \psi & \textsf{PL} \\
4 & & \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \Box \psi & \textsf{RK} \ 3 \\
5 & & \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to (\Box \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 2, 4\\
\end{array}

:::

## necessity commutes with conjunction ($\Leftarrow$) {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_K (\Box \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) \to \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi)$
:::


::: {.proof}
$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & & (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \varphi & \textsf{PL} \\
2 & & \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \Box \varphi & \textsf{RK} \ 1 \\
3 & & (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \psi & \textsf{PL} \\
4 & & \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \Box \psi & \textsf{RK} \ 3 \\
5 & & \Box (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to (\Box \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 2, 4\\
\end{array}
$$
:::




## possibility commutes with disjunction ($\Rightarrow$) {.smaller}


::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_K \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) \to (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi)$
:::


::: {.proof}
$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & & \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) \to \neg (\neg \Box \neg \varphi \vee \neg \Box \neg \psi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond \\
2 & & \neg (\neg \Box \neg \varphi \vee \neg \Box \neg \psi) \to (\Box \neg \varphi \wedge \Box \neg \psi) & \textsf{PL} \\
3 & & (\Box \neg \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) \to \Box (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) & \textsf{Prop} \ 7.6\\
4 & & \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) \to \Box (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 1, 2, 3\\
5 & & (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) \to \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{PL} \\
6  & & \Box (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) \to \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{RK} \ 5 \\
7 & & \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) \to \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 4, 6\\
8 & & \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \neg \neg \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{PL} \\
9 & & \neg \neg \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \neg \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond\\
10 &  & \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) \to \neg \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) &  \textsf{PL} \ 7, 8, 9\\
11 & & \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) \to (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 10
\end{array}
$$

:::


## possibility commutes with disjunction ($\Leftarrow$) {.smaller}


::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_K (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) \to \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi)$
:::

::: {.proof}
$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & & \neg \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \neg \neg \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond\\
2 & & \neg \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 1\\
3 & & \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) \to (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) & \textsf{PL}\\
4 & & \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \Box (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) & \textsf{RK} \ 3\\
5 & & \Box (\neg \varphi \wedge \neg \psi) \to (\Box \neg \varphi \wedge \Box \neg \psi) & \textsf{Prop} \ 7.5\\
6 & & (\Box \neg \varphi \wedge \Box \neg \psi)  \to \neg (\neg \Box \neg \varphi \vee \neg \Box \neg \psi) & \textsf{PL} \\
7 & & \neg (\neg \Box \neg \varphi \vee \neg \Box \neg \psi)  \to \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond\\
8 & & \Box \neg (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 5, 6, 7\\
9 & & \neg \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) \to \neg (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 2, 8\\
10 & & (\Diamond \varphi \vee \Diamond \psi) \to \Diamond (\varphi \vee \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 9\\
\end{array}
$$
:::


## one more helpful theorem {.smaller}

::: {.theorem}
$\vdash_K (\Diamond \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) \to \Diamond (\varphi \wedge \psi)$
:::

::: {.proof}
$$
\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & & \neg (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to (\psi \to \neg \varphi) & \textsf{PL} \\
2 & & \Box \neg (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to \Box (\psi \to \neg \varphi) & \textsf{RK} \ 1 \\
3 & & \Box (\psi \to \neg \varphi) \to (\Box \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi) &  \textsf{K}[\psi/p, \neg \varphi/q] \\
4 & & \Box \neg (\varphi \wedge \psi) \to (\Box \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi)  & \textsf{PL} \ 2, 3\\
5 & & \neg (\Box  \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi) \to \neg \Box \neg (\varphi \wedge \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 4 \\
6 & & \neg (\Box  \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi) \to \Diamond (\varphi \wedge \psi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond \\
7 & & (\Box \psi \wedge \neg \Box \neg \varphi) \to \neg (\Box \psi \to \Box \neg \varphi) & \textsf{PL} \\
8 & & (\Box \psi \wedge \neg \Box \neg \varphi) \to \Diamond (\varphi \wedge \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 6, 7\\
9 & & (\Box \psi \wedge \Diamond \varphi) \to (\Box \psi \wedge \neg \Box \neg \varphi) & \textsf{Def} \ \Diamond\\
10 & & (\Diamond \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) \to (\Box \psi \wedge \Diamond \varphi) & \textsf{PL} \\
11 & & (\Diamond \varphi \wedge \Box \psi) \to \Diamond (\varphi \wedge \psi) & \textsf{PL} \ 8, 9, 10\\
\end{array}
$$
:::
